implementation_notes: Sequence's protocol extensions provide default implementations of map, compactMap, filter, reduce and lazy for every sequence, so a chain of stage closures over a sequence is the standard pipeline and replaces the classic stage-list class (developer.apple.com Sequence). Stages that can fail use throws/rethrows or Result along the same chain. Combine publishers are the asynchronous counterpart; for in-memory data the sequence chain is simpler.
pitfalls: Each map/filter materialises an array unless .lazy is inserted, so a long chain allocates one intermediate collection per stage.
.lazy returns a lazy sequence whose operations stay lazy only until an eager operation runs, so a later first/last silently pulls the whole chain.
A throwing stage forces try through the chain and the first failure aborts the rest, losing partial results unless stages return Result.

variants.name: Combine publisher operator pipeline
variants.implementation_notes: Combine chains Publisher operators: each operator returns a new publisher that subscribes to its upstream when the pipeline is completed by a subscriber, so publisher.filter.map.sink is the pipeline and demand (backpressure) is negotiated explicitly (Apple developer docs). This is the realization for asynchronous event streams - network responses, timers, UI state - and it replaces the hand-written stage list and driver for that domain. Keep the sequence chain for synchronous data.
pitfalls: Nothing runs until a subscriber attaches, and forgetting to retain the AnyCancellable cancels the pipeline immediately.
Publisher operator types are deeply nested, so long chains slow down type checking and are hard to name.
An error completes the pipeline: without catch/replaceError one failing stage stops all downstream processing.
